{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen.

ANTHONY, 2026-09-23, in his own words: "What I was thinking would be nice for somebody to just publish requirements (in reflow2 graph form). For instance, my brother wants to build a shop in Kennewick, WA. Maybe a template for building a shop in Kennewick WA could be just the requirements for building a shop. Then my brother just uploads the requirements template and builds whatever he likes (as long as it meets all the requirements of a shop in Kennewick)." He tied it to the templates idea and to the x-dimension discussion of 2026-09-22.

⭐⭐ WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT "TEMPLATE", AND IT IS THE WHOLE CONTENT OF THE IDEA. The template ideas recorded so far (`dec:idea-a-domain-seed-template-starts-a-design-in-the-fields-own-shape`, `dec:idea-an-org-template-carries-the-approved-references-a-design-must-use`) are about a SEED: structure copied into a new design, which the user then owns and edits. This one is the opposite kind of thing: OBLIGATIONS the user does NOT own and cannot edit — only satisfy. The publisher says WHAT must hold; the brother decides HOW (post-frame or stick-built, one bay or three) and the design is judged only on whether every published requirement is met. That is solution-neutral requirements, which is the systems-engineering meaning of a requirement in the first place.

⭐⭐ AND reflow2 ALREADY HAS THE VOCABULARY FOR EXACTLY THIS, WITH THIS EXACT CITY IN IT. `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` records the founding operating-environment document (2026-07-17): "A house in Kennewick WA must meet city ordinances, county rules, state requirements, building and fire codes, seismic provisions and occupancy limits". Its schema keeps three kinds of rule apart, and the third is this idea precisely: `Constraint` is self-imposed, `DesignRule` is a chosen convention, and `EnvironmentRule` is EXTERNALLY IMPOSED — "the design cannot negotiate it, only comply, seek a variance, or fail". The shapes are all declared: `Project OPERATES_IN Environment`, `Environment IMPOSES EnvironmentRule`, `COMPLIES_WITH` / `VIOLATES_RULE`, with a confirmed violation standing for an accepted variance. The half that locates a design (`Environment`, `DEPLOYED_TO`) is built; the compliance half never was, and `decision:vocab:environment` parks it "deliberately unused until a user asks for it". ⇒ THIS IS THE FIRST TIME A REAL USER HAS ASKED, with a real site and a real builder. The parking note said a real request should pull it back in.

⭐ AND IT IS THE x-DIMENSION WITH A PUBLISHER WHO IS NOT THE BUILDER. `dec:idea-design-is-composable-on-two-axes-authority-and-role` defines x as one design holding intent and others each holding a realisation of it, and sharpens it to "design is not always the same users" (A5 writes requirements; others build to them). A Kennewick shop template is that axis in plain form: the city, or whoever transcribes its rules, is the requirements organisation; the brother is the one implementation; a neighbour building a different shop is a rival implementation of the same requirements, comparable on the same denominator.

📌 AND THE JURISDICTIONS STACK, which puts the y-axis back in. A shop in Kennewick answers to more than one publisher at once: the city, the county, the state's adopted building code, and possibly the utility and a homeowners' association. Those publishers form an authority hierarchy of their own. So the example again touches both axes: the brother's design SATISFIES across x, and what it satisfies is a stack ordered down y. (Illustrative: which bodies actually impose what on a Kennewick shop is NOT checked here, and must not be read as a statement of the code.)

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) REFERENCE, NOT COPY. The requirements live in the publisher's own design, marked published; the brother's design declares a pinned dependency on it (`external_dependency` / `mirrors`, "designed against your published surface at this version") and satisfies those requirements from his side. When the publisher revises, his design learns it from the pin. ⚠️ Blocked today by the same missing piece as both axes: SATISFIES cannot cross a graph boundary (`create_edge` resolves both endpoints in scope), `export_surface` carries no Verifications, `mirror_surface`'s refresh is recorded as broken, and reflow2 itself publishes 0 of its own requirements.

(b) COPY IN, WITH A PIN. `/genesis` (or `import_graph` / `merge_designs`) brings the published requirements into the brother's own design, marked with a provenance that can never read as his own word (the seed-template node already noted `provenance: imported` as the hook) and pinned to the template version, so a later version can be compared (`compare_designs`) and the difference offered to him. Works with what exists today, and within one graph SATISFIES, verification and closure all work. ⚠️ Counter: a copy is a second home for the publisher's facts — the one-fact-one-home problem the hub work named — and it goes stale silently unless the pin is read.

(c) THE REQUIREMENTS ARRIVE AS ENVIRONMENT RULES. The template is an Environment ("Kennewick, WA") that IMPOSES EnvironmentRules; the brother's Project OPERATES_IN it; compliance is recorded per rule as COMPLIES_WITH or VIOLATES_RULE (a confirmed violation being a variance). This builds the parked layer and uses its variance lifecycle, which is better thought through than much of what ships. It composes with (a) or (b) as to WHERE the rules live. ⚠️ Counter: it splits "requirements" in two — a builder's own requirements and the imposed ones behave differently — which is the point, but is a second concept a user has to learn.

(d) THE SIMPLEST THING: A REQUIREMENTS-ONLY DESIGN, SHARED AS A FILE. Somebody writes "shop in Kennewick" as an ordinary reflow2 design with Requirements and no build, publishes the export, and the brother imports it as the start of his. No new mechanism at all; the question becomes only how to tell imported requirements from his own. Closest to how he described it ("uploads the requirements template"), and the cheapest experiment that would show whether the rest is needed.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used against it:

🛑 CODES ARE CONDITIONAL, AND A FLAT LIST WILL NOT SERVE. Real building rules apply only if the design crosses a threshold (floor area, height, use, occupancy, distance to a property line). A template that states every rule unconditionally either buries the builder or is wrong; one that states applicability has to evaluate it against his design. So a requirement needs an "applies when" that reads the design, and nothing in reflow2 models applicability today.

🛑 AUTHORITY. The city's code is the law; a reflow2 template is somebody's transcription of it. "My design meets the Kennewick shop template" is not "my design will get a permit", and the gap between those is exactly `dec:idea-who-warrants-a-domain-template-and-how-does-it-stay-current`: who wrote it, from which edition, and how a design learns the code changed. A transcription that reads as authoritative is the dangerous kind.

🛑 SCALE AND WHO MAINTAINS IT. Adopted building codes are very large. The realistic first template is small and hand-picked (setbacks, height, permit triggers, the few structural and electrical rules a shop meets), which is useful and must say it is partial, or a builder reads "met all of them" as "met the code".

⚠️ AND THE STANDING OVER-DESIGN WARNING, which is Anthony's own: option (d) needs nothing built, and the first real Kennewick shop would say which of (a)–(c) is actually needed.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — is a template, at its simplest, just a PUBLISHED SET OF REQUIREMENTS that somebody else satisfies however they like — "the requirements for a shop in Kennewick, WA" — rather than a seed that copies a field's shape into a new design?","rationale":"Captured under the brainstorm skill, after searching first. The search found four close neighbours, all open or parked, and the finding that makes this worth recording separately is that the new framing joins them: the template ideas were about seeding SHAPE, the x-axis idea was about a design that holds only intent, and the environment layer was designed for externally imposed rules using this same city as its worked example. A published requirements template is where all three meet, and the parked vocabulary had been waiting for exactly this kind of real request.

Kept as a new node rather than a sharpening of the seed-template node, because it is a different kind of template (obligations you satisfy, not structure you own), with a different staleness profile and a different mechanism.

Authored by Anthony (who:ajs); the example is his brother's real plan. Nothing about Kennewick's actual code was looked up or is asserted here.","status":"proposed"}
